        sql << "," << w.quote(scopeOptions.scope);
    if (hasCheckpointEvalId)
        sql << "," << MetricSql(w, scopeOptions.checkpointEvalId);
    if (hasCheckpointEpoch)
        sql << "," << MetricSql(w, scopeOptions.checkpointEpoch);
    if (hasParentExperimentId)
        sql << "," << MetricSql(w, scopeOptions.parentExperimentId);
    sql << ") ";

    if (scopeOptions.scope == "checkpoint")
    {
        sql << "ON CONFLICT (checkpoint_eval_id) WHERE analysis_scope = 'checkpoint' AND checkpoint_eval_id IS NOT NULL DO UPDATE SET ";
    }
    else if (hasAnalysisScope)
    {
        sql << "ON CONFLICT (experiment_id, model_id) WHERE analysis_scope = 'final' DO UPDATE SET ";
    }
    else
    {
        sql << "ON CONFLICT (experiment_id, model_id) DO UPDATE SET ";
    }
    sql
        << "symbol = EXCLUDED.symbol, "
        << "prediction_horizon = EXCLUDED.prediction_horizon, "
        << "target_epochs = EXCLUDED.target_epochs, "
        << "completed_epochs = EXCLUDED.completed_epochs, "
        << "train_accuracy = EXCLUDED.train_accuracy, "
        << "validation_accuracy = EXCLUDED.validation_accuracy, "
        << "infer_accuracy = EXCLUDED.infer_accuracy, "
        << "actual_down_count = EXCLUDED.actual_down_count, "
        << "actual_neutral_count = EXCLUDED.actual_neutral_count, "
        << "actual_up_count = EXCLUDED.actual_up_count, "
        << "pred_down_count = EXCLUDED.pred_down_count, "
        << "pred_neutral_count = EXCLUDED.pred_neutral_count, "
        << "pred_up_count = EXCLUDED.pred_up_count, "
        << "confusion_down_down = EXCLUDED.confusion_down_down, "
        << "confusion_down_neutral = EXCLUDED.confusion_down_neutral, "
        << "confusion_down_up = EXCLUDED.confusion_down_up, "
        << "confusion_neutral_down = EXCLUDED.confusion_neutral_down, "
        << "confusion_neutral_neutral = EXCLUDED.confusion_neutral_neutral, "
        << "confusion_neutral_up = EXCLUDED.confusion_neutral_up, "
        << "confusion_up_down = EXCLUDED.confusion_up_down, "
        << "confusion_up_neutral = EXCLUDED.confusion_up_neutral, "
        << "confusion_up_up = EXCLUDED.confusion_up_up, "
        << "accept_count = EXCLUDED.accept_count, "
        << "accept_rate = EXCLUDED.accept_rate, "
        << "accept_accuracy = EXCLUDED.accept_accuracy, "
        << "reject_count = EXCLUDED.reject_count, "
        << "loss_last = EXCLUDED.loss_last, "
        << "best_metric_name = EXCLUDED.best_metric_name, "
        << "best_metric_value = EXCLUDED.best_metric_value, "
        << "leader_score = EXCLUDED.leader_score, "
        << "analysis_status = EXCLUDED.analysis_status, "
        << "analysis_notes = EXCLUDED.analysis_notes, "
        << "source_train_log_path = EXCLUDED.source_train_log_path, "
        << "source_infer_log_path = EXCLUDED.source_infer_log_path, "
        << "updated_at = now()";
    if (hasAnalysisScope)
        sql << ", analysis_scope = EXCLUDED.analysis_scope";
    if (hasCheckpointEvalId)
        sql << ", checkpoint_eval_id = EXCLUDED.checkpoint_eval_id";
    if (hasCheckpointEpoch)
        sql << ", checkpoint_epoch = EXCLUDED.checkpoint_epoch";
    if (hasParentExperimentId)
        sql << ", parent_experiment_id = EXCLUDED.parent_experiment_id";
    sql << ";";
    w.exec(sql.str());
}

template <typename Value>
void PrintOptional(std::ostream& output, const std::optional<Value>& value)
{
    if (value) output << *value;
    else output << "null";
}

void PrintOptionalText(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::optional<std::string>& value)
{
    if (value) output << RecommendationMachineText(*value);
    else output << "null";
}

void PrintOptionalPercent(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::optional<double>& value)
{
    if (!value)
    {
        output << "null";
        return;
    }
    const auto flags = output.flags();
    const auto precision = output.precision();
    output.imbue(std::locale::classic());
    output << std::fixed << std::setprecision(6) << *value;
    output.flags(flags);
    output.precision(precision);
}

void PrintDiagnostics(
    std::ostream& output,
    const std::vector<std::string>& diagnostics)
{
    if (diagnostics.empty())
    {
        output << "none";
        return;
    }
    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < diagnostics.size(); ++index)
    {
        if (index != 0) output << '|';
        output << RecommendationMachineText(diagnostics[index]);
    }
}

              "automatic_follow_up=false,campaign_state_row_created=false,"

}

        output << ",execution_evidence_count=" << member.executionEvidenceCount
               << ",activation_evidence_count=" << member.activationEvidenceCount;
        output << ",symbol=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.symbol);
        output << ",prediction_horizon=";
        PrintOptional(output, member.predictionHorizon);
        output << ",execution_state="
               << RecommendationCampaignStatusExecutionStateText(
                      member.executionState)
               << ",activation_state="
               << RecommendationCampaignStatusActivationStateText(
                      member.activationState)
               << ",operational_state="
               << RecommendationCampaignStatusOperationalStateText(
                      member.operationalState)
               << ",terminal_result="
               << RecommendationCampaignStatusTerminalResultText(
                      member.terminalResult)
               << ",status=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.status);
        output << ",phase=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.phase);
        output << ",current_epoch=";
        PrintOptional(output, member.currentEpoch);
        output << ",target_epochs=";
        PrintOptional(output, member.targetEpochs);
        output << ",worker_pid=";
        PrintOptional(output, member.workerPid);
        output << ",current_operation=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.currentOperation);
        output << ",worker_started_at=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.workerStartedAt);
        output << ",started_at=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.startedAt);
        output << ",completed_at=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.completedAt);
        output << ",exit_code=";
        PrintOptional(output, member.exitCode);
        output << ",error_message=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.errorMessage);
        output << ",model_id=";
        PrintOptional(output, member.modelId);
        output << ",invocation_identity_hash=";
        PrintOptionalText(output, member.invocationIdentityHash);
        output << ",model_link_count=" << member.modelLinkCount
               << ",final_inference_result_count="
               << member.finalInferenceResultCount
               << ",completed_final_inference_result_count="
               << member.completedFinalInferenceResultCount
               << ",failed_final_inference_result_count="
               << member.failedFinalInferenceResultCount
               << ",final_analysis_result_count="
               << member.finalAnalysisResultCount
               << ",completed_final_analysis_result_count="
               << member.completedFinalAnalysisResultCount
               << ",failed_final_analysis_result_count="
               << member.failedFinalAnalysisResultCount;
        output << ",train_complete=" << (member.trainComplete ? "true" : "false")
               << ",infer_configured=" << (member.inferConfigured ? "true" : "false")
               << ",infer_complete=" << (member.inferComplete ? "true" : "false")
               << ",analyze_configured=" << (member.analyzeConfigured ? "true" : "false")
               << ",analyze_complete=" << (member.analyzeComplete ? "true" : "false")
               << ",consistency_status="
               << RecommendationCampaignStatusConsistencyText(member.consistency)
               << ",diagnostic=";
        PrintDiagnostics(output, member.diagnosticCodes);
        output << ',';
        PrintSafety(output);
        output << '\n';
    }
}

} // namespace

int RunRecommendationCampaignStatusCommand(
    const std::string& connectionString,
    const RecommendationCampaignStatusRequest& request,
    std::ostream& output,
    std::ostream& errors)
{
    try
    {
        const auto normalized = NormalizeRecommendationCampaignStatusRequest(request);
        pqxx::connection connection{connectionString};
        PrintSnapshot(
            output, ReadRecommendationCampaignStatusSnapshot(connection, normalized));
        return 0;
    }
    catch (const std::exception& error)
    {
        errors << "RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_STATUS_FAILED"
               << ",materialization_id=" << request.materializationId
               << ",materialization_contract_version=null,"
                  "materialization_identity_hash=null,status_contract_version="
               << kRecommendationCampaignStatusContractVersion
               << ",snapshot_identity_hash=null,observed_at=null,"
                  "aggregate_status=inconsistent,consistency_status=inconsistent,"
                  "diagnostic="
               << RecommendationMachineText(error.what())
               << ",member_count=0,proposal_only_count=0,executed_count=0,"
                  "activated_count=0,paused_count=0,pending_count=0,"
                  "running_count=0,running_train_count=0,running_infer_count=0,"
                  "running_analyze_count=0,completed_count=0,failed_count=0,"
                  "cancelled_count=0,inconsistent_count=0,terminal_count=0,"
                  "nonterminal_count=0,active_worker_count=0,"
                  "minimum_current_epoch=null,maximum_current_epoch=null,"
                  "total_current_epochs=null,total_target_epochs=null,"
                  "completed_percent=null,terminal_percent=null,";
        PrintSafety(errors);
        errors << '\n';
        return 1;
    }
}

     2	=============================================================
     3	
     4	Purpose and authority
     5	---------------------
     6	
     7	Phase 5 Step 4 is a read-only point-in-time projection for one persisted Phase
     8	4D campaign materialization. It reports every exact member's ordinary Phase 4C
     9	review, execution, activation, experiment lifecycle, worker metadata, model,
    10	final inference, and final analysis evidence. It creates no campaign status or
    11	lifecycle authority and persists nothing.
    12	
    13	The immutable ordered rows in
    14	``experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member`` are the only
    15	membership source. The production Phase 4D loader validates the manifest,
    16	canonical identity and hash, selected count, contiguous ordinals, unique links,
    17	and exact proposal provenance before downstream status is projected.
    18	
    19	Snapshot and query contract
    20	---------------------------
    21	
    22	One PostgreSQL ``REPEATABLE READ``, ``READ ONLY`` transaction owns the complete
    23	snapshot. The operation takes no advisory or row locks, performs no write or
    24	sequence call, and uses bounded exact-ID queries for the materialized proposals
    25	and their linked experiments. Unrelated workflow and experiment rows cannot
    26	become campaign members.
    27

    29	row. It is metadata, not identity. The deterministic version-1 snapshot

    34	Persisted lifecycle timestamps are evidence and are bound; ``observed_at`` and
    35	local wall-clock time are not identity inputs. The identity contains no random
    36	value, local command process ID, transaction ID, or unordered iteration. A
    37	persisted ``worker_pid`` is bound as database evidence but is not treated as a

    53	final analysis. Successful ``completed/done`` therefore requires the exact
    54	final inference row selected by the scheduler (current model, symbol, horizon,
    55	threshold, and dates) and completed final analysis for the current model. A
    56	persisted ``completed/done`` recommendation-conversion experiment without that
    57	configured pipeline is reported as inconsistent rather than treated as a
    58	train-only success.

    61	execution, missing experiments, incompatible activation/lifecycle state,
    62	incoherent worker evidence, and missing configured terminal results remain
    63	visible as deterministic member diagnostics. A valid materialization still
    64	returns every ordered member when downstream evidence is malformed. An invalid
    65	materialization rejects the command because exact membership cannot be trusted.
    66	Any inconsistent member forces aggregate ``inconsistent`` status.

     1	Phase 4D Step 5 — Campaign Handoff Status
     2	===========================================
     3	
     4	Purpose and boundary
     5	--------------------
     6	
     7	Step 5 projects one immutable Phase 4D campaign materialization onto the
     8	current Phase 4C proposal lifecycle. The materialization manifest and its
     9	one-based ordered member links remain the sole authority for campaign
    10	membership. Current proposal review, execution, activation, and experiment
    11	lifecycle rows are observed; they are never changed or repaired.
    12	
    13	The projection is not persisted authority and is not authorization. In
    14	particular, ``ready_for_phase4c_execution`` and
    15	``ready_for_phase4c_activation`` mean only that the observed durable
    16	prerequisites appear satisfied. Existing explicit Phase 4C commands remain
    17	responsible for review, execution, and activation.
    18	
    19	State and precedence
    20	--------------------
    21	
    22	Every materialization member is reported in its stored ordinal order with its
    23	linked proposal, greatest-ID review decision, execution, activation, existing
    24	Phase 4C workflow state, and deterministic integrity diagnostics. Aggregate
    25	state uses this precedence:
    26	
    27	1. any integrity diagnostic: ``inconsistent``;
    28	2. any latest rejection: ``review_rejected``;
    29	3. no approvals: ``awaiting_phase4c_review``;
    30	4. mixed approvals and unreviewed members: ``partially_reviewed``;
    31	5. all approved with no executions: ``ready_for_phase4c_execution``;
    32	6. some executions: ``partially_executed``;
    33	7. all executed with no activations: ``ready_for_phase4c_activation``;
    34	8. some activations: ``partially_activated``;
    35	9. all activated: ``fully_activated``.
    36	
    37	Review timestamps do not select the current decision. Consistent with Phase
    38	4C Step 3, the greatest review-decision primary key is authoritative.
    39	``awaiting_review`` and ``no_authoritative_review`` count members for which no
    40	valid current review can be established, including a member whose linked
    41	proposal is missing. Such malformed members also carry an integrity diagnostic,
    42	so these counts cannot cause an aggregate awaiting/ready state.
    43	
    44	Integrity diagnostics
    45	---------------------
    46	
    47	Malformed immutable materialization evidence—unsupported contract version,
    48	member-count mismatch, non-contiguous or reordered ordinals, invalid canonical
    49	hashes, or duplicate immutable links—causes detailed inspection to fail
    50	closed. Downstream inconsistencies remain observable with stable codes. These
    51	include a missing linked proposal; proposal ID, recommendation, source
    52	experiment, canonical identity, or hash mismatch; invalid latest review;
    53	execution without valid approval; duplicate execution or activation rows;
    54	activation without execution; execution/activation provenance or identity
    55	mismatch; missing linked experiment; and incompatible experiment lifecycle.
    56	No diagnostic path mutates data.
    57	
    58	Read consistency and queries
    59	----------------------------
    60	
    61	Each command uses one PostgreSQL ``read_transaction`` set to
    62	``REPEATABLE READ`` before its first query, so all manifest, member, and
    63	workflow reads use one consistent snapshot. Show uses the existing validated
    64	Step 4 mapping for one manifest and its members, then one bounded Phase 4C
    65	workflow query for its exact linked proposal IDs. List first loads its bounded
    66	manifest set, then performs one Step 4 member query and one workflow query per
    67	returned materialization. The default list limit is 100 and the enforced
    68	maximum is 1000. This avoids per-member workflow queries and preserves the
    69	authoritative member order. No migration, view, lock, sequence access, or new
    70	privilege is added.
    71	
    72	CLI
    73	---
    74	
    75	::
    76	
    77	   LSTM_Release --show-recommendation-campaign-handoff=ID
    78	   LSTM_Release --list-recommendation-campaign-handoffs \
    79	     --campaign-handoff-limit=100
    80	
    81	The show command emits one ``RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_HANDOFF`` summary followed
    82	by one ``RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_HANDOFF_MEMBER`` row per stored member. The
    83	bounded list emits deterministic materialization-ID order and a final count.
    84	Output states ``read_only=true`` and explicitly reports that no
    85	materialization, proposal, review, execution, activation, experiment,
    86	scheduler, or worker was created or started. Summary, list-completion, and
    87	error rows carry the complete safety field set; member rows repeat
    88	``read_only=true`` and are contextual children of the show summary.
    89	
    90	Verification and deferred work
    91	------------------------------
    92	
    93	Use an explicit disposable non-``LSTM`` database::
    94	
    95	   createdb phase4d_campaign_test 2>/dev/null || true

   338	
   339	RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus AggregateState(
   340	    const RecommendationCampaignStatusSnapshot& result)
   341	{
   342	    const int count = static_cast<int>(result.members.size());
   343	    if (result.inconsistentCount > 0)
   344	        return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::inconsistent;
   345	    if (result.executedCount == 0)
   346	        return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::notExecuted;
   347	    if (result.executedCount < count)
   348	        return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::partiallyExecuted;
   349	    if (result.activatedCount < count)
   350	        return result.activatedCount == 0
   351	            ? RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::executedPaused
   352	            : RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::partiallyActivated;
   353	    if (result.terminalCount == count)
   354	    {
   355	        if (result.completedCount == count)
   356	            return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::completed;
   357	        if (result.cancelledCount == count)
   358	            return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::cancelled;
   359	        if (result.failedCount > 0 && result.cancelledCount == 0)
   360	            return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::completedWithFailures;
   361	        return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::mixedTerminal;
   362	    }
   363	    if (result.runningCount > 0)
   364	        return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::inProgress;
   365	    if (result.pendingCount > 0)
   366	        return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::queued;
   367	    return RecommendationCampaignAggregateStatus::executedPaused;
   368	}

    37	std::map<long long, RecommendationCampaignStatusExperimentEvidence>
    38	LoadExperimentEvidence(
    39	    pqxx::transaction_base& transaction,
    40	    const std::vector<long long>& experimentIds,
    41	    const std::map<long long, std::string>& expectedInvocationByExperiment)
    42	{
    43	    if (experimentIds.empty()) return {};
    44	    std::vector<long long> ids = experimentIds;
    45	    std::sort(ids.begin(), ids.end());
    46	    if (std::adjacent_find(ids.begin(), ids.end()) != ids.end())
    47	        throw std::runtime_error("campaign_status_duplicate_experiment_link");
    48	
    49	    pqxx::params parameters;
    50	    std::ostringstream placeholders;
    51	    for (std::size_t index = 0; index < ids.size(); ++index)
    52	    {
    53	        if (index != 0) placeholders << ',';
    54	        placeholders << '$' << index + 1;
    55	        parameters.append(ids[index]);
    56	    }
    57	    const std::size_t timeZoneParameter = ids.size() + 1;
    58	    parameters.append(kRecommendationDateTimeZone);
    59	    const std::string query = std::string{R"SQL(
    60	SELECT e.experiment_id,e.symbol,e.prediction_horizon,e.status,e.phase,
    61	       e.target_epochs,e.current_epoch,e.worker_pid,e.current_operation,
    62	       e.worker_started_at::text AS worker_started_at,
    63	       e.started_at::text AS started_at,e.completed_at::text AS completed_at,
    64	       e.exit_code,e.error_message,e.last_model_id,e.invocation_mode,
    65	       e.duplicate_nonce,e.c_next_threshold,e.core_lr_mult,e.head_lr_mult,
    66	       e.checkpoint_interval,
    67	       to_char(e.train_start AT TIME ZONE )SQL"} +
    68	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
    69	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD') AS train_start,
    70	       to_char(e.train_end AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
    71	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
    72	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD') AS train_end,
    73	       to_char(e.infer_start AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
    74	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
    75	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD') AS infer_start,
    76	       to_char(e.infer_end AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
    77	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
    78	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD') AS infer_end,e.resume_model_id,
    79	       e.infer_start IS NOT NULL AS infer_start_present,
    80	       e.infer_end IS NOT NULL AS infer_end_present,
    81	       (e.infer_start IS NOT NULL AND e.infer_end IS NOT NULL) AS infer_configured,
    82	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
    83	         (SELECT count(*) FROM model mo
    84	           WHERE mo.model_id=e.last_model_id AND mo.experiment_id=e.experiment_id)
    85	       END AS model_link_count,
    86	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
    87	         (SELECT count(*) FROM inference_eval_result ir
    88	           WHERE ir.model_id=e.last_model_id AND ir.inference_scope='final'
    89	             AND ir.checkpoint_eval_id IS NULL AND ir.symbol=e.symbol
    90	             AND ir.prediction_horizon=e.prediction_horizon
    91	             AND ir.threshold_logret=e.c_next_threshold
    92	             AND ir.from_date=to_char(e.infer_start AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
    93	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
    94	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD')
    95	             AND ir.to_date=to_char(e.infer_end AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
    96	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
    97	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD'))
    98	       END AS inference_result_count,
    99	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
   100	         (SELECT count(*) FROM inference_eval_result ir
   101	           WHERE ir.model_id=e.last_model_id AND ir.inference_scope='final'
   102	             AND ir.checkpoint_eval_id IS NULL AND ir.symbol=e.symbol
   103	             AND ir.prediction_horizon=e.prediction_horizon
   104	             AND ir.threshold_logret=e.c_next_threshold
   105	             AND ir.from_date=to_char(e.infer_start AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
   106	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
   107	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD')
   108	             AND ir.to_date=to_char(e.infer_end AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
   109	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
   110	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD')
   111	             AND ir.status='completed')
   112	       END AS completed_inference_result_count,
   113	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
   114	         (SELECT count(*) FROM inference_eval_result ir
   115	           WHERE ir.model_id=e.last_model_id AND ir.inference_scope='final'
   116	             AND ir.checkpoint_eval_id IS NULL AND ir.symbol=e.symbol
   117	             AND ir.prediction_horizon=e.prediction_horizon
   118	             AND ir.threshold_logret=e.c_next_threshold
   119	             AND ir.from_date=to_char(e.infer_start AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
   120	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
   121	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD')
   122	             AND ir.to_date=to_char(e.infer_end AT TIME ZONE )SQL" +
   123	        "$" + std::to_string(timeZoneParameter) +
   124	        R"SQL(,'YYYY-MM-DD')
   125	             AND ir.status='failed')
   126	       END AS failed_inference_result_count,
   127	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN
   128	         (SELECT count(*) FROM experiment_analysis_result ar
   129	           WHERE ar.experiment_id=e.experiment_id AND ar.analysis_scope='final')
   130	       ELSE
   131	         (SELECT count(*) FROM experiment_analysis_result ar
   132	           WHERE ar.experiment_id=e.experiment_id AND ar.model_id=e.last_model_id
   133	             AND ar.analysis_scope='final') END
   134	         AS analysis_result_count,
   135	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
   136	         (SELECT count(*) FROM experiment_analysis_result ar
   137	           WHERE ar.experiment_id=e.experiment_id AND ar.model_id=e.last_model_id
   138	             AND ar.analysis_scope='final' AND ar.analysis_status='completed') END
   139	         AS completed_analysis_result_count,
   140	       CASE WHEN e.last_model_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE
   141	         (SELECT count(*) FROM experiment_analysis_result ar
   142	           WHERE ar.experiment_id=e.experiment_id AND ar.model_id=e.last_model_id
   143	             AND ar.analysis_scope='final' AND ar.analysis_status='failed') END
   144	         AS failed_analysis_result_count
   145	FROM experiment e
   146	WHERE e.experiment_id IN ()SQL" + placeholders.str() +
   147	        ") ORDER BY e.experiment_id;";
   148	    const pqxx::result rows = transaction.exec(query, parameters);
   149	
   150	    std::map<long long, RecommendationCampaignStatusExperimentEvidence> result;
   151	    for (const auto& row : rows)
   152	    {
   153	        RecommendationCampaignStatusExperimentEvidence value;
   154	        value.experimentId = row["experiment_id"].as<long long>();
   155	        value.symbol = row["symbol"].as<std::string>();
   156	        value.predictionHorizon = row["prediction_horizon"].as<int>();
   157	        value.status = row["status"].as<std::string>();
   158	        value.phase = row["phase"].as<std::string>();
   159	        value.targetEpochs = row["target_epochs"].as<int>();
   160	        value.currentEpoch = OptionalValue<int>(row, "current_epoch");
   161	        value.workerPid = OptionalValue<int>(row, "worker_pid");
   162	        value.currentOperation = OptionalText(row, "current_operation");
   163	        value.workerStartedAt = OptionalText(row, "worker_started_at");
   164	        value.startedAt = OptionalText(row, "started_at");
   165	        value.completedAt = OptionalText(row, "completed_at");
   166	        value.exitCode = OptionalValue<int>(row, "exit_code");
   167	        value.errorMessage = OptionalText(row, "error_message");
   168	        value.modelId = OptionalValue<long long>(row, "last_model_id");
   169	        value.invocationMode = row["invocation_mode"].is_null()
   170	            ? std::string{} : row["invocation_mode"].as<std::string>();
   171	        value.duplicateNonce = row["duplicate_nonce"].as<long long>();
   172	        ExperimentInvocationConfiguration invocation;
   173	        invocation.configuration.symbol = value.symbol;
   174	        invocation.configuration.predictionHorizon = value.predictionHorizon;
   175	        invocation.configuration.labelThreshold =
   176	            row["c_next_threshold"].as<double>();
   177	        invocation.configuration.coreLrMult =
   178	            OptionalValue<double>(row, "core_lr_mult");
   179	        invocation.configuration.headLrMult =
   180	            OptionalValue<double>(row, "head_lr_mult");
   181	        invocation.configuration.targetEpochs = value.targetEpochs;
   182	        invocation.configuration.trainStartDate =

   189	        value.invocationIdentityCanonical =

   191	        const auto expected = expectedInvocationByExperiment.find(value.experimentId);
   192	        value.invocationProvenanceValid =

   196	        value.inferEndPresent = row["infer_end_present"].as<bool>();
   197	        value.inferConfigured = row["infer_configured"].as<bool>();

  4972	std::optional<std::string> ValidateSchedulerControlTransition(const SchedulerOptions& options,
  4973	                                                                     const SchedulerControlExperimentRow& row,
  4974	                                                                     std::string& newStatus,
  4975	                                                                     std::string& newPhase)
  4976	{
  4977	    newStatus = row.status;
  4978	    newPhase = row.phase;
  4979	
  4980	    if (options.pauseExperimentId.has_value())
  4981	    {
  4982	        if (row.status != "pending")
  4983	            return "pause_requires_pending_status";
  4984	        newStatus = "paused";
  4985	        return std::nullopt;
  4986	    }
  4987	    if (options.resumeExperimentId.has_value())
  4988	    {
  4989	        if (row.status != "paused")
  4990	            return "resume_requires_paused_status";
  4991	        newStatus = "pending";
  4992	        return std::nullopt;
  4993	    }
  4994	    if (options.cancelExperimentId.has_value())
  4995	    {
  4996	        if (row.status == "running")
  4997	            return "running_experiment_cannot_be_cancelled";
  4998	        if (row.status != "pending" && row.status != "paused")
  4999	            return "cancel_requires_pending_or_paused_status";
  5000	        newStatus = "cancelled";
  5001	        return std::nullopt;
  5002	    }
  5003	    if (options.retryFailedExperimentId.has_value())
  5004	    {
  5005	        if (row.status != "failed")
  5006	            return "retry_requires_failed_status";
  5007	        newStatus = "pending";
  5008	        newPhase = RetryPhaseForExperiment(row);
  5009	        return std::nullopt;
  5010	    }
  5011	    if (options.requeueAnalysisExperimentId.has_value())
  5012	    {
  5013	        if (row.status == "running")
  5014	            return "running_experiment_cannot_be_requeued";
  5015	        if (!ControlModelId(row).has_value())
  5016	            return "requeue_analysis_requires_model_id";
  5017	        newStatus = "pending";
  5018	        newPhase = "analyze";
  5019	        return std::nullopt;
  5020	    }
  5021	    if (options.requeueInferenceExperimentId.has_value())
  5022	    {
  5023	        if (row.status == "running")
  5024	            return "running_experiment_cannot_be_requeued";
  5025	        if (!ControlModelId(row).has_value())
  5026	            return "requeue_inference_requires_model_id";
  5027	        newStatus = "pending";
  5028	        newPhase = "infer";
  5029	        return std::nullopt;
  5030	    }
  5031	
  5032	    return "unknown_scheduler_control_action";
  5033	}

  5035	void ApplySchedulerControlTransition(pqxx::work& w,
  5036	                                            const std::string& action,
  5037	                                            const SchedulerControlExperimentRow& row,
  5038	                                            const std::string& newStatus,
  5039	                                            const std::string& newPhase)
  5040	{
  5041	    std::ostringstream sql;

  5043	        << ", phase = " << w.quote(newPhase)
  5044	        << ", updated_at = now()";
  5045	
  5046	    if (action == "cancel")
  5047	    {
  5048	        sql << ", completed_at = now()";
  5049	    }
  5050	    else if (action == "retry_failed" ||
  5051	             action == "requeue_analysis" ||
  5052	             action == "requeue_inference")
  5053	    {
  5054	        sql << ", started_at = NULL"
  5055	            << ", worker_started_at = NULL"
  5056	            << ", completed_at = NULL"

  5058	            << ", error_message = NULL"
  5059	            << ", worker_pid = NULL"
  5060	            << ", current_operation = NULL";
  5061	    }
  5062	
  5063	    sql << " WHERE experiment_id = " << row.experimentId << ";";
  5064	    w.exec(sql.str());

 14122	bool SignalProcessForStop(const SchedulerStopCandidate& candidate,
 14123	                                 bool force,
 14124	                                 std::string& errorMessage,
 14125	                                 bool& usedSigkill)
 14126	{
 14127	    usedSigkill = false;
 14128	    if (!candidate.pid.has_value())
 14129	    {
 14130	        errorMessage = "pid_not_found";
 14131	        return false;
 14132	    }
 14133	
 14134	    const pid_t pid = static_cast<pid_t>(*candidate.pid);
 14135	    const long long experimentId = candidate.experiment.experiment.experimentId;
 14136	    if (!ProcessStillExists(pid))
 14137	        return true;
 14138	
 14139	    std::cout << "SCHEDULER_STOP_SIGNAL"
 14140	              << ",experiment_id=" << experimentId
 14141	              << ",pid=" << pid
 14142	              << ",signal=SIGTERM"
 14143	              << std::endl;
 14144	    if (::kill(pid, SIGTERM) != 0 && errno != ESRCH)
 14145	    {
 14146	        errorMessage = "sigterm_failed";
 14147	        return false;
 14148	    }
 14149	    if (WaitForProcessExit(pid))
 14150	        return true;
 14151	
 14152	    if (!force)
 14153	    {
 14154	        errorMessage = "process_still_running";
 14155	        return false;
 14156	    }
 14157	
 14158	    std::cout << "SCHEDULER_STOP_SIGNAL"
 14159	              << ",experiment_id=" << experimentId
 14160	              << ",pid=" << pid
 14161	              << ",signal=SIGKILL"
 14162	              << std::endl;
 14163	    usedSigkill = true;
 14164	    if (::kill(pid, SIGKILL) != 0 && errno != ESRCH)
 14165	    {
 14166	        errorMessage = "sigkill_failed";
 14167	        return false;
 14168	    }
 14169	    if (WaitForProcessExit(pid))
 14170	        return true;
 14171	
 14172	    errorMessage = "process_still_running";
 14173	    return false;
 14174	}

 14340	SchedulerStatusCounts LoadSchedulerStatusCounts(pqxx::work& w)

 14344	        "SELECT status, count(*) "
 14345	        "FROM experiment "
 14346	        "GROUP BY status;");

 14348	    {

 14350	        const int count = row[1].as<int>();
 14351	        if (status == "pending")
 14352	            counts.queued = count;
 14353	        else if (status == "paused")
 14354	            counts.paused = count;
 14355	        else if (status == "running")
 14356	            counts.running = count;
 14357	        else if (status == "completed")
 14358	            counts.completed = count;
 14359	        else if (status == "failed")
 14360	            counts.failed = count;
 14361	        else if (status == "cancelled")
 14362	            counts.cancelled = count;
 14363	    }

/bin/bash -lc "nl -ba \"docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0004-scheduler-ownership-boundaries.md\" | sed -n '20,85p'" in /Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor
 succeeded in 0ms:
    20	
    21	## 2. Decision
    22	
    23	The scheduler owns only explicitly assigned lifecycle work classes.
    24	
    25	- Eligibility and lifecycle transitions are durable database contracts.
    26	- The scheduler atomically claims bounded work before launching a worker.
    27	- Worker launch and execution occur outside database transactions.
    28	- Workers perform one bounded operation and report facts; they do not select or
    29	  queue further work independently.
    30	- Capacity, retries, recovery, shutdown, and operator controls are defined per
    31	  work class.
    32	- New scheduler-managed work requires an ADR defining eligibility, claim,
    33	  capacity, idempotency, recovery, observability, and regression boundaries.
    34	- Recommendation generation, scoring, and review remain outside scheduler
    35	  polling under ADR-0003.
    36	
    37	## 3. Rationale and decision drivers
    38	
    39	- Prevent duplicate workers and lost lifecycle updates.
    40	- Keep database transactions short.
    41	- Make capacity and process ownership observable and recoverable.
    42	- Prevent unrelated explicit commands from becoming background automation.
    43	
    44	## 4. Consequences
    45	
    46	### 4.1 Positive consequences
    47	
    48	- Clear ownership between lifecycle services, scheduler, and workers.
    49	- Narrow database claims support multiple processes safely.
    50	- Scheduler capacity remains predictable.
    51	- Orphan recovery can reconcile durable attempt state with processes.
    52	
    53	### 4.2 Negative consequences and trade-offs
    54	
    55	- Every work class needs explicit claim/recovery design.
    56	- Process supervision and database reconciliation remain operationally complex.
    57	- New automation cannot be added merely by placing a command in the poll loop.
    58	
    59	### 4.3 Risks and mitigations
    60	
    61	- Launch after claim fails: persist a distinct launch failure and reconcile.
    62	- Multiple schedulers race: use database-visible conditional claims/locks.
    63	- Stale PIDs: combine attempt identity and durable timestamps/state with process
    64	  inspection; never trust PID alone.
    65	
    66	## 5. Compatibility and migration
    67	
    68	This ADR records existing scheduler boundaries and requires no schema change.
    69	Future work classes may require additive attempt/capacity schema and must
    70	preserve current experiment and continuation behavior.
    71	
    72	## 6. Verification and operational evidence
    73	
    74	- Pure eligibility, capacity, command, and status-mapping tests.
    75	- Claim/concurrency tests with multiple database connections.
    76	- Launch-failure, completion-race, orphan-recovery, and shutdown tests.
    77	- Regression checks proving advisory commands do not enter scheduler polling.
    78	- Controlled integration that does not disturb running experiments.
    79	
    80	## 7. Alternatives considered
    81	
    82	### 7.1 Workers self-select follow-up work
    83	
    84	Rejected because it bypasses centralized capacity, durable lifecycle ownership,
    85	and operator controls.

-- Phase 4A Step 3 hardening.  This migration is intentionally additive: 026
-- remains the creation/legacy-upgrade migration, while these constraints make
-- status metadata symmetric for all newly inserted or updated rows.  NOT VALID
-- avoids guessing or rewriting any legacy Phase 4 prototype history.

DO $$
BEGIN
    IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
        WHERE conname = 'experiment_recommendation_scan_source_filter_positive_check'
    ) THEN
        ALTER TABLE experiment_recommendation_scan
            ADD CONSTRAINT experiment_recommendation_scan_source_filter_positive_check
            CHECK (source_experiment_filter IS NULL OR source_experiment_filter > 0)
            NOT VALID;
    END IF;

    IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
        WHERE conname = 'experiment_recommendation_scan_failed_error_nonempty_check'
    ) THEN
        ALTER TABLE experiment_recommendation_scan
            ADD CONSTRAINT experiment_recommendation_scan_failed_error_nonempty_check
            CHECK (status <> 'failed' OR btrim(error_message) <> '')
            NOT VALID;
    END IF;

    IF NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM pg_constraint
        WHERE conname = 'experiment_recommendation_status_metadata_symmetric_check'
    ) THEN
        ALTER TABLE experiment_recommendation
            ADD CONSTRAINT experiment_recommendation_status_metadata_symmetric_check
            CHECK (
                (
                    (status = 'rejected'
                     AND rejected_at IS NOT NULL
                     AND rejected_reason IS NOT NULL
                     AND btrim(rejected_reason) <> '')
                    OR
                    (status <> 'rejected'
                     AND rejected_at IS NULL
                     AND rejected_reason IS NULL)
                )
                AND (
                    (status = 'expired' AND expired_at IS NOT NULL)
                    OR
                    (status <> 'expired' AND expired_at IS NULL)
                )
                AND (
                    (status = 'approved' AND approved_experiment_id IS NOT NULL)
                    OR
                    (status <> 'approved' AND approved_experiment_id IS NULL)
                )
            ) NOT VALID;
    END IF;
END $$;

## Current Phase 5 boundary

The implemented authority and data flow is:

```text
immutable ranking snapshot
  → read-only campaign plan
  → read-only campaign review
  → immutable explicit campaign approval/rejection
  → immutable materialization manifest and ordered members
  → ordinary Phase 4C proposal reviews
  → ordinary Phase 4C executions creating paused experiments
  → ordinary Phase 4C activations making experiments pending
  → existing scheduler lifecycle
  → final inference and analysis evidence
  → read-only Phase 5 operational status
```

The exact boundaries are:

- The materialization manifest and ordered member rows are the sole campaign-membership authority. Rankings, policies, recommendations, current queries, experiment lineage, and continuation descendants cannot add members.
- Current Phase 4C review authority remains the greatest review-decision ID for each proposal.
- Phase 4C execution rows remain the durable authority linking proposals and approving reviews to paused experiments.
- Phase 4C activation rows remain the durable authority for the exact `paused/train → pending/train` transition.
- Phase 5 Steps 1–3 are atomic conveniences over those existing authorities. They introduce no campaign execution, activation, launch, or lifecycle table. [Step 3’s contract](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/docs/Phase5ExperimentRecommendationCampaignLaunch.rst:7>) explicitly leaves durable authority in materialization, Phase 4C, and experiment rows.
- The scheduler sees ordinary `experiment` rows only. It does not consume campaign, proposal, review, execution, or activation tables.
- The scheduler owns claims, process launch, completion, recovery, and capacity. Recommendation and campaign code must not become a second scheduler.
- Step 4 reads one repeatable-read snapshot, takes no locks, and treats `worker_pid` only as persisted evidence—not process-liveness proof. [The status contract](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/docs/Phase5ExperimentRecommendationCampaignStatus.rst:7>) establishes these rules.
- Step 4 classifies terminal state and validates the presence/cardinality of final results, but its public model contains only final-result counts and completion flags—not result IDs or research metrics. [The current status model](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentRecommendationCampaignStatus.hpp:79>) stops at those counts.
- Continuation automation remains independent. Any continuation child is a new ordinary experiment and is not silently added to immutable materialization membership.

## Remaining operational gap

The most important remaining gap is not campaign execution control; it is the missing research outcome projection.

After Step 4 reports that a campaign completed, an operator still cannot ask one bounded campaign command:

- which exact final inference and analysis rows belong to each member;
- how those results compare with the frozen source evidence that originally justified the recommendation;
- which parameter was changed and from what value to what value;
- which completed members lack usable metrics;
- which comparisons changed the evaluation context;
- whether unrelated experiments or historical models were excluded; or
- what deterministic campaign-level outcome identity represents that evidence.

The necessary source baseline already exists in recommendation rows—leader score, inference accuracy, predicted-neutral proportion, source experiment/model/analysis, and the mutation specification. Campaign planning already reads that frozen evidence. [The planning repository](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentRecommendationCampaignPlanningRepository.cpp:143>) demonstrates its authoritative mapping.

Campaign-wide controls are valuable eventually, but they are not the safest next increment. Existing controls have action-specific semantics: pause accepts only pending, resume only paused, cancel rejects running, and retry accepts only failed. [Current control validation](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentScheduler.cpp:4972>) confirms this. More importantly, the scheduler currently loads pending work and later performs an unconditional running-state update by experiment ID, creating an observe-then-update window that must be hardened before a campaign pause can safely race scheduler claims. [The launch-state update](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentScheduler.cpp:11485>) does not condition on the row still being pending.

## Candidate comparison

| Candidate | User value and architectural fit | Schema and scheduler coupling | Partial/terminal behavior and concurrency | Retry, size, tests, duplicate authority | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Read-only campaign outcome assessment** | High research value; directly extends Step 4 using existing evidence and exact membership. | No schema; no scheduler coupling. | Repeatable-read snapshot, no locks; nonterminal, failed, cancelled, completed, and inconsistent members are reported separately. | Deterministic evidence hash; same evidence gives the same hash. Medium implementation/test burden. No lifecycle authority. | **Preferred Phase 5 Step 5.** |
| Campaign pause/resume/cancel/retry/stop | High operational value, but five materially different lifecycle actions do not form one narrow contract. | A safe, auditable design likely needs shared lifecycle primitives and operation audit; stop also couples to process supervision. | Pause/cancel race claims; running stop cannot be transactionally rolled back; mixed member states force either low-value all-or-nothing rejection or unsafe partial application. | Action-specific idempotency is currently absent. Large implementation and very high concurrency/process test burden. High duplicate-authority risk if implemented in campaign code. | Defer until lifecycle and scheduler claim hardening; split by action. |
| Reconciliation or repair | Useful only after a concrete diagnosed inconsistency. Step 4 already supplies reconciliation diagnostics. | Generic repair would need privileged mutation and repair audit; scheduler coupling varies by defect. | Immutable Phase 4C evidence cannot safely be “repaired” generically; partial/terminal rules are defect-specific. | No defensible generic retry identity. Large test matrix and high authority risk. | Reject generic repair; design only for a proven corruption class. |
| Persisted campaign lifecycle authority | Could coordinate operator intent and display a durable campaign state. | New state/event schema and eventual scheduler integration required. | Must reconcile every per-experiment transition, retry, cancellation, recovery, and continuation race. | Very large state-machine and migration burden. Directly duplicates Volume VII/XI authority. | Defer to controlled research automation, not Phase 5. |
| Scheduler-aware admission/capacity | Valuable for budgets, priority, or campaign concurrency limits. | Requires scheduler claim/query changes, schema/indexes, and an ADR under the accepted scheduler boundary. | Must arbitrate overlapping campaigns, unrelated pending work, capacity races, and recovery. | Very large scheduler regression burden; admission retry requires durable reservations. | Defer to Volume XI/Volume X design. |
| Bounded automatic progression | Convenience from review/materialization through launch or follow-up. | Requires durable requests/budgets and scheduler or background-loop integration. | Partial progress and failures require reconciliation; hidden scans risk repeated or unauthorized action. | Large implementation; request-ledger idempotency required. Risks second lifecycle authority and collapses explicit confirmations. | Reject for Phase 5; belongs in future Volume X work after ADRs. |
| Persisted terminal completion/failure summary | Strong eventual audit value. | New append-only snapshot/member schema; no direct scheduler coupling. | “Terminal” is not final because failed experiments can be retried and cancelled work may later require replacement. One snapshot becomes stale; multiple snapshots require explicit historical semantics. | Medium-large migration/test burden; evidence-hash retries are feasible. No lifecycle duplication if strictly historical. | Defer until the read-only outcome contract and experiment-finality semantics are proven. |
| Stop after Step 4 | Zero implementation risk. | None. | Leaves current member lifecycle untouched. | No tests or authority risk. | Rejected because the exact-result research gap can be closed safely without mutation. |

## Recommended Phase 5 Step 5

**Title:** Deterministic Recommendation Campaign Outcome Assessment

**One-sentence purpose:** Read one exact materialized campaign and deterministically compare its frozen recommendation baselines with its observed final inference and analysis outcomes, without mutating lifecycle state or making causal, authorization, or profitability claims.

**Why this direction wins:** It closes the recommendation-to-result research loop, uses evidence already produced by the system, and avoids the unresolved scheduler, process, audit, and finality problems attached to control or persistence proposals.

**Why it belongs in Phase 5:** Phase 5 already owns explicit campaign execution, activation, launch, and operational observation; assessing the resulting exact experiments is the bounded research-facing completion of that path.

**Why it is safe now:** It can reuse Step 4 membership/lifecycle validation and perform additional exact-ID reads in the same repeatable-read transaction. It needs no schema, no live process information, no scheduler changes, and no additional experiment evidence to define or test the contract.

## Proposed contract

### Command

Both forms are accepted:

```text
LSTM_Release --recommendation-campaign-outcome=MATERIALIZATION_ID
LSTM_Release --recommendation-campaign-outcome MATERIALIZATION_ID
```

Contract rules:

- One positive materialization ID is required.
- Duplicate forms and combinations with any other standalone operation are rejected before database dispatch.
- There are no filters and no list command in Step 5; this prevents broad scans.
- `--yes` is rejected because the command is read-only.
- `--dry-run` is rejected because the command is intrinsically a dry read.
- No operator, reason, score threshold, or profitability option is accepted.

### Membership authority

Membership is exactly the stored one-based ordinal sequence in:

- `experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization`; and
- `experiment_recommendation_campaign_materialization_member`.

The existing materialization validator must establish:

- supported contract version;
- valid canonical/hash pair;
- positive member count of at most 1000;
- count agreement;
- contiguous ordinals;
- unique member, ranking-member, and proposal links; and
- exact recommendation, source-experiment, and proposal provenance.

Continuation children, replacement experiments, semantic duplicates, current ranking output, and inferred proposal matches are excluded.

### Eligibility and evidence rules

The inspection command is valid at any campaign progress state. Research metrics are available for a member only when:

1. Step 4 classifies its downstream evidence as consistent;
2. it is terminal `completed/done`;
3. it has exactly one current model linked to the experiment;
4. it has exactly one completed final inference row matching current model, symbol, horizon, threshold, inference dates, final scope, and null checkpoint linkage;
5. it has exactly one completed final analysis row matching experiment, current model, and final scope;
6. the materialized recommendation and proposal still match their stored provenance; and
7. required numeric values are finite.

The frozen source baseline comes from the persisted recommendation, not by reopening and recomputing the source experiment:

- source experiment/model/analysis IDs;
- source leader score;
- source inference accuracy;
- optional source predicted-neutral proportion;
- source evidence count;
- changed parameter;
- source and proposed canonical values; and
- source/proposed invocation identities.

The observed result side reports:

- campaign experiment and model IDs;
- exact final inference-result ID and accuracy;
- exact final analysis ID;
- leader score;
- inference accuracy;
- derived predicted-neutral proportion and evidence count; and
- result timestamps and identity/provenance fields.

### Comparison context

Each successful member is classified as:

- `same_evaluation_context` when source and proposed symbol, horizon, label threshold, and inference date range match; or
- `changed_evaluation_context` otherwise.

Raw source and outcome metrics remain visible in both cases. Leader-score and inference-accuracy delta classifications are included in campaign aggregates only for `same_evaluation_context`; Step 5 does not pretend cross-horizon or cross-threshold values are directly comparable.

### Per-member outcomes

Each member has exactly one outcome:

- `not_ready`: proposal-only, paused, pending, running, or paused after progress;
- `succeeded_comparable`: completed with complete metrics and the same evaluation context;
- `succeeded_context_changed`: completed with metrics but changed evaluation context;
- `succeeded_metric_gap`: valid completed lifecycle/result rows but leader score or inference accuracy is unavailable;
- `terminal_failed`: valid failed lifecycle;
- `terminal_cancelled`: valid cancelled lifecycle; or
- `inconsistent`: invalid membership-adjacent or downstream provenance/cardinality/lifecycle/result evidence.

A failed or cancelled member is an observed research outcome, not an integrity error.

### Aggregate outcome precedence

1. Any inconsistent member: `inconsistent`.
2. Any nonterminal member: `not_ready`.
3. All cancelled: `cancelled`.
4. All succeeded with complete metrics: `completed`.
5. All succeeded but at least one metric gap: `completed_with_metric_gaps`.
6. All terminal, with at least one failure and no cancellation: `completed_with_failures`.
7. Any other all-terminal mixture: `mixed_terminal`.

The aggregate also reports comparable/context-changed/metric-gap counts and positive/zero/negative delta counts for leader score and inference accuracy. It does not compute a campaign score, weighted mean, statistical significance, profitability, or authorization decision.

### Identity and retry contract

Outcome contract version 1 canonically binds:

- materialization ID, version, identity, and ordered membership;
- the Step 4 status snapshot identity;
- frozen recommendation source evidence;
- proposal mutation and invocation evidence;
- exact result IDs, statuses, timestamps, and metric values;
- per-member outcome, comparison context, and diagnostics; and
- aggregate counts.

`observed_at`, local time, process ID, transaction ID, and row-return order are excluded.

An exact retry over unchanged durable evidence produces the same outcome identity hash. If scheduler state or result evidence changes, the command produces a new point-in-time identity. No duplicate row can be created because nothing is persisted.

### Explicit non-goals

Step 5 does not:

- approve, reject, execute, activate, pause, resume, cancel, retry, stop, or repair anything;
- persist a completion or outcome row;
- close a campaign or prevent later experiment retries;
- follow continuation or lineage children;
- query process tables or infer liveness;
- poll, signal, start, stop, or configure the scheduler;
- create a profitability or causal-improvement claim;
- use outcome metrics as authorization;
- scan unrelated campaigns or experiments; or
- automatically invoke any earlier or later command.

## Transaction and concurrency model

One PostgreSQL `READ ONLY`, `REPEATABLE READ` transaction owns the complete operation.

The repository should:

1. load and validate the materialization;
2. build the existing Step 4 status snapshot inside the same transaction;
3. load recommendation and proposal evidence using exact member IDs;
4. load exact final inference rows using the bounded experiment/model/configuration set;
5. load exact final analysis rows using the bounded experiment/model set; and
6. build the pure outcome assessment.

The query count must be fixed with respect to member count—no per-member database loop. All `IN`/`VALUES` inputs are bounded by 1000 exact immutable members.

Locking order is **none**:

- no advisory locks;
- no row locks;
- no table locks requested by application code.

A concurrent scheduler transition or result update is either visible throughout the snapshot or invisible throughout it. The command never returns a hybrid of before/after evidence. It may become stale immediately after the transaction ends.

Invalid materialization evidence prevents a trusted membership set and fails the command. Downstream inconsistency remains observable for every exact member and does not trigger repair. Any exception ends the read transaction with no state to roll back.

## Scheduler and worker boundary

The command reads persisted experiment and result evidence only.

It does not:

- read scheduler process lists;
- inspect `/proc`, `ps`, or child-process state;
- signal any PID;
- trust `worker_pid` as proof of liveness;
- reserve capacity;
- alter polling eligibility;
- create claims; or
- update experiment state.

This preserves ADR-0004, which requires new scheduler-managed behavior to define eligibility, capacity, recovery, idempotency, and observability explicitly. [ADR-0004](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/docs/architecture/adr/ADR-0004-scheduler-ownership-boundaries.md:21>) also forbids trusting PID evidence alone.

Campaign lifecycle controls should remain deferred until scheduler claim updates are conditional/atomic and lifecycle mutations are exposed through shared audited primitives. Running stop is especially unsuitable for campaign atomicity because the existing implementation signals processes one at a time and persists each cancellation separately. [Current stop behavior](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentScheduler.cpp:14248>) is intentionally best-effort, not rollback-capable.

## Schema and privilege impact

- No migration.
- No new table, sequence, index, view, trigger, function, or campaign state.
- No new runtime grant.
- The command uses existing `SELECT` capability for materialization, recommendations, proposals, workflow evidence, experiments, models, final inference results, and final analysis results.
- No sequence is read for allocation or advanced.
- Existing result rows remain their current mutable operational records. The outcome identity is therefore a point-in-time assessment, not immutable result history.

A schema-presence check should fail clearly if required existing columns or final-result scope migrations are missing.

## CLI and machine output

Successful output begins with:

```text
RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_OUTCOME
```

followed by one row per exact ordinal:

```text
RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_OUTCOME_MEMBER
```

Failure emits:

```text
RECOMMENDATION_CAMPAIGN_OUTCOME_FAILED
```

The summary should include:

- materialization, status-snapshot, and outcome identities;
- `observed_at`;
- aggregate outcome and Step 4 operational status;
- terminal, nonterminal, completed, failed, cancelled, inconsistent, comparable, context-changed, and metric-gap counts;
- delta-sign counts;
- deterministic diagnostics; and
- explicit safety fields.

Member rows should include:

- all immutable membership/provenance IDs;
- operational and terminal state;
- mutation parameter and canonical source/proposed values;
- source experiment/model/analysis evidence and metrics;
- result experiment/model/inference/analysis IDs and metrics;
- comparison context and deltas;
- outcome state, consistency, and diagnostics.

Optional values use `null`; variable text uses the existing machine percent encoder. Every row should state:

```text
transaction_read_only=true
snapshot_isolation=repeatable_read
advisory_locks_acquired=0
row_locks_acquired=0
rows_inserted=0
rows_updated=0
rows_deleted=0
sequences_advanced=0
scheduler_polled=false
scheduler_signaled=false
worker_processes_inspected=false
workers_signaled=false
profitability_evaluated=false
authorization_granted=false
automatic_follow_up=false
```

## Test and regression plan

No tests were run during this planning task.

Required implementation verification:

- **Pure domain tests**
  - request normalization and 1000-member bound;
  - ordinal and ID alignment;
  - every per-member state;
  - aggregate precedence;
  - source/proposed comparison-context classification;
  - null, non-finite, mismatched, and contradictory metrics;
  - deterministic canonical identity under shuffled input;
  - `observed_at` exclusion;
  - metric/result/status changes altering identity;
  - exact zero/positive/negative delta classification.

- **Repository tests on an explicit disposable non-`LSTM` database**
  - exact materialization membership only;
  - unrelated campaign, experiment, model, inference, and analysis rows ignored;
  - exact final-inference identity selection;
  - current-model final-analysis selection;
  - historical models and checkpoint results ignored;
  - missing, duplicate, failed, or wrong-provenance result diagnostics;
  - failed, cancelled, partially progressed, and mixed-terminal campaigns;
  - repeatable-read stability across concurrent updates;
  - changed snapshot after a later transaction;
  - runtime read-only behavior;
  - unchanged table digests, `updated_at` values, and sequence state;
  - concurrent writers not blocked by application locks.

- **Service and CLI tests**
  - stable summary/member/error output;
  - percent encoding and `null`;
  - both option forms;
  - duplicate option rejection;
  - positive-ID validation;
  - rejection of `--yes`, `--dry-run`, and other standalone operations;
  - no-list/no-filter behavior.

- **Regression suites**
  - `ExperimentRecommendationCampaignStatusTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationCampaignStatusRepositoryTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationCampaignMaterializationTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationCampaignMaterializationRepositoryTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationCampaignHandoffTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationCampaignHandoffRepositoryTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationConversionWorkflowTests`
  - `ExperimentRecommendationConversionWorkflowRepositoryTests`
  - all Phase 5 execution, activation, and launch pure/repository suites
  - recommendation repository/persistence tests for frozen source evidence
  - `SchedulerChildStatusTests` and release CLI dispatch checks to prove no scheduler behavior changed

## Implementation increments

This should be one logical Phase 5 step delivered as three reviewable commits. It needs no schema-only increment, should begin with a pure-domain increment, and should not be postponed for live experiment evidence.

- **Regression:** All Phase 5 suites plus CLI dispatch and scheduler child-status tests.
- **Completion:** Documentation, help, parser, service, and repository agree exactly; output explicitly denies mutation, scheduler, worker, profitability, and authorization effects.
- **Commit:** `Phase 5 Step 5: Add recommendation campaign outcome assessment`

## Deferred and rejected alternatives

- Campaign controls should be deferred and later designed as separate pause, resume, cancel, retry, and stop capabilities—not one omnibus Step 5. They first require shared per-experiment lifecycle primitives, durable audit semantics, conditional scheduler claims, and action-specific concurrency tests.
- Running campaign stop should not promise atomicity. Process signals are irreversible external effects and require a durable request plus compensating/reconciliation protocol.
- Generic repair is rejected. Step 4 already identifies inconsistencies; a repair command should be designed only for a specific reproduced corruption class.
- Persisted campaign lifecycle state, scheduler admission, budget reservations, and automatic progression belong to future Volume X/XI architecture and require ADRs.
- An immutable outcome-snapshot table is deferred until retry/replacement/finality semantics are decided and the read-only outcome schema has been exercised.
- Moving immediately to another phase would leave a safe, high-value research gap unresolved.

## Remaining risks and unresolved questions

Resolved from current code and documentation:

- Membership authority is the immutable materialization, not experiments or rankings.
- Frozen source metrics come from persisted recommendation evidence.
- Final results are selected using the current campaign experiment model and the scheduler’s exact final inference/final analysis identity.
- Failed and cancelled members are valid terminal outcomes.
- `worker_pid` is persisted evidence only.
- Continuation descendants are outside campaign membership.
- No profitability evidence exists, so no profitability conclusion is permitted.

Genuinely unresolved—and intentionally excluded from Step 5:

1. **Outcome finality:** failed experiments are retryable and result rows are operationally mutable/upserted. The repository supplies no authoritative “campaign closed forever” event. Step 5 must therefore remain a point-in-time assessment.
2. **Scientific aggregation policy:** the repository defines no accepted weighting, materiality threshold, significance test, or rule for cross-horizon/cross-threshold comparisons. Step 5 should expose raw metrics, explicit context, and conservative delta counts only.
3. **Safe bulk lifecycle mutation:** scheduler claim hardening and a shared audited lifecycle service do not yet exist. This blocks a safe campaign pause/resume/cancel/retry design.
4. **Historical snapshot retention:** there is no decision on whether outcome snapshots should be unique per materialization, append for every changed evidence identity, or require explicit campaign closure. Persistence should wait for that decision.

Implementation should begin now with the pure-domain increment; it does not need a migration or live campaign evidence.

## Current Phase 5 boundary

The implemented authority and data flow is:

```text
immutable ranking snapshot
  → read-only campaign plan
  → read-only campaign review
  → immutable explicit campaign approval/rejection
  → immutable materialization manifest and ordered members
  → ordinary Phase 4C proposal reviews
  → ordinary Phase 4C executions creating paused experiments
  → ordinary Phase 4C activations making experiments pending
  → existing scheduler lifecycle
  → final inference and analysis evidence
  → read-only Phase 5 operational status
```

The exact boundaries are:

- The materialization manifest and ordered member rows are the sole campaign-membership authority. Rankings, policies, recommendations, current queries, experiment lineage, and continuation descendants cannot add members.
- Current Phase 4C review authority remains the greatest review-decision ID for each proposal.
- Phase 4C execution rows remain the durable authority linking proposals and approving reviews to paused experiments.
- Phase 4C activation rows remain the durable authority for the exact `paused/train → pending/train` transition.
- Phase 5 Steps 1–3 are atomic conveniences over those existing authorities. They introduce no campaign execution, activation, launch, or lifecycle table. [Step 3’s contract](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/docs/Phase5ExperimentRecommendationCampaignLaunch.rst:7>) explicitly leaves durable authority in materialization, Phase 4C, and experiment rows.
- The scheduler sees ordinary `experiment` rows only. It does not consume campaign, proposal, review, execution, or activation tables.
- The scheduler owns claims, process launch, completion, recovery, and capacity. Recommendation and campaign code must not become a second scheduler.
- Step 4 reads one repeatable-read snapshot, takes no locks, and treats `worker_pid` only as persisted evidence—not process-liveness proof. [The status contract](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/docs/Phase5ExperimentRecommendationCampaignStatus.rst:7>) establishes these rules.
- Step 4 classifies terminal state and validates the presence/cardinality of final results, but its public model contains only final-result counts and completion flags—not result IDs or research metrics. [The current status model](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentRecommendationCampaignStatus.hpp:79>) stops at those counts.
- Continuation automation remains independent. Any continuation child is a new ordinary experiment and is not silently added to immutable materialization membership.

## Remaining operational gap

The most important remaining gap is not campaign execution control; it is the missing research outcome projection.

After Step 4 reports that a campaign completed, an operator still cannot ask one bounded campaign command:

- which exact final inference and analysis rows belong to each member;
- how those results compare with the frozen source evidence that originally justified the recommendation;
- which parameter was changed and from what value to what value;
- which completed members lack usable metrics;
- which comparisons changed the evaluation context;
- whether unrelated experiments or historical models were excluded; or
- what deterministic campaign-level outcome identity represents that evidence.

The necessary source baseline already exists in recommendation rows—leader score, inference accuracy, predicted-neutral proportion, source experiment/model/analysis, and the mutation specification. Campaign planning already reads that frozen evidence. [The planning repository](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentRecommendationCampaignPlanningRepository.cpp:143>) demonstrates its authoritative mapping.

Campaign-wide controls are valuable eventually, but they are not the safest next increment. Existing controls have action-specific semantics: pause accepts only pending, resume only paused, cancel rejects running, and retry accepts only failed. [Current control validation](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentScheduler.cpp:4972>) confirms this. More importantly, the scheduler currently loads pending work and later performs an unconditional running-state update by experiment ID, creating an observe-then-update window that must be hardened before a campaign pause can safely race scheduler claims. [The launch-state update](</Volumes/Developer SSD/ExpertAdvisor/Sources/ExperimentScheduler.cpp:11485>) does not condition on the row still being pending.
